material_title: 3 Drills to Improve Timing and Load When Hitting
extracted_text: Early hitting is usually caused by loading too early, which causes moving forward too early, early hip extension, and lunging at the ball.
final_claim_text: Hitters who consistently swing early often initiate their load prematurely, a pattern that frequently co-occurs with an uncontrolled forward move, early back-hip extension, and lunging into contact.
observable_evidence: Hitter shifting weight forward well before pitch release, back hip extending early, and body posture lunging toward the ball — a co-occurring pattern, not asserted as a single-cause diagnosis.
applies_when: A hitter is consistently early on pitches and lunging forward into contact.
does_not_apply_when: A hitter is late on pitches or failing to initiate stride in time.
source_side_caveat: The source presents a coaching heuristic. The final wording records association/co-occurrence and does not claim validated causation.

material_title: Two Tee Extension Drill with Megan Rembielak using a Tanner Tee | Softball Hitting Drills
extracted_text: Extension after contact keeps the barrel through the tunnel toward the pitcher, maximizing power and helping direct the ball rather than rolling over into weak grounders.
final_claim_text: Extending the bat barrel through the hitting zone tunnel toward the pitcher after contact optimizes directional ball flight and power while preventing premature wrist rollover.
observable_evidence: Bat barrel path continuing forward through and beyond contact toward the pitcher before the finish roll-over; this is barrel-path direction, not a prescription to cast or force generic arm extension.
coaching_cue: Drive the barrel through the tunnel from home to the pitcher.
applies_when: Executing swing follow-through and extension on pitches through the middle and outer parts of the zone.
does_not_apply_when: Adjusting to extreme inside pitch locations where hand path must clear tightly without full forward barrel extension.
source_side_caveat: TannerTees is the commercial publishing channel and Megan Rembielak/MegRem is the featured instructor. Scope remains softball-only; source inclusion does not imply broad publisher trust.

extracted_text: Hitters move back and forth between three different plate locations to learn how swing timing and tempo need to adjust for pitch distance.
final_claim_text: Moving hitters between three different plate distances during toss drills trains their ability to adjust swing timing and rhythm relative to pitch arrival time.
observable_evidence: A hitter taking swings sequentially from three different home-plate markers at varied distances from the front-toss screen.
applies_when: Practicing timing rhythm and reaction-time adjustments during front toss or live pitching practice.
does_not_apply_when: Isolating stationary swing mechanics on a tee where pitch arrival time is not a factor.
source_side_caveat: The source is a short softball drill clip. This record does not broaden the publisher's trust, prescribe universal mechanics, or assert baseball applicability.

material_title: Youth Practice Plan Series | Hitting Tips
extracted_text: When setting up a tee, pitch location dictates contact-point depth relative to the body (away off lead hip, middle off front foot, inside in front of front foot) to maintain connection.
final_claim_text: Adjust contact points on a batting tee according to pitch location: outside pitches off the lead hip, middle pitches off the lead foot, and inside pitches out in front of the lead foot.
observable_evidence: Positioning of the batting tee relative to the hitter's front foot and lead hip across controlled pitch-location setups.
coaching_cue: Outside off lead hip, middle off lead foot, inside out front.
applies_when: Setting up batting-tee drills for specific pitch-location practice.
does_not_apply_when: Practicing dynamic pitch recognition or live-pitching hitting without controlled tee setups.
source_side_caveat: This is a controlled tee-setup convention, not an immutable universal contact-point law. ABCA is the verified uploader; Golden Spikes branding remains source-context metadata rather than broader trust evidence.

material_title: Youth Practice Plan Series | Hitting Tips
extracted_text: Jumping back into a med-ball toss teaches lower-half loading into the back hip while keeping weight inside the back knee to ground forces effectively.
final_claim_text: Using a jump-back medicine-ball toss with an age-appropriate light medicine ball (approximately 2–4 lbs for youth players) teaches hitters to load into the back hip and maintain weight on the inside of the back knee.
observable_evidence: Hitter jumping back onto the rear leg, hinging at the back hip without the knee collapsing outward, before throwing the medicine ball.
coaching_cue: Jump back and load into your back hip.
applies_when: Developing dynamic lower-half loading and back-hip weight distribution using an age-appropriate light medicine ball of approximately 2–4 lbs for youth players.
does_not_apply_when: Players lack basic lower-body balance, have joint issues requiring physical screening, or only adult-weight medicine balls are available.
numeric_evidence_ref: Gemini-verified source video 7J-JoyaSabA at 00:58–02:30 explicitly states the 2–4 lb youth medicine-ball guidance.
source_side_caveat: This remains a source-specific youth drill prescription with an equipment guardrail; it is not a universal loading mechanic or a statement that every youth player is physically ready for the drill.

extracted_text: Hitters must rotate the torso to bring the pipe around to the tee, avoiding diving the chest forward at the ball.
final_claim_text: Hitters should adjust swing plane to different pitch locations through torso rotation and body posture rather than diving their chest forward toward the ball.
observable_evidence: Maintaining spinal posture during torso rotation, with the chest not lunging forward toward the ball, across different controlled tee locations.
source_coaching_cue: Rotate around your center so the pipe comes to the tee—don't dive your chest forward.
coaching_cue_policy: Preserve as source-specific internal-focus example phrasing only; do not treat it as HitterLoop's default generated cue language.
applies_when: Working on swing plane control, torso rotation, and pitch-location adjustment in the demonstrated tee/PVC drill context.
does_not_apply_when: Full game situations where timing and stride dynamics vary unpredictably, or when treating the source's internal-focus cue as a universal cueing policy.
source_side_caveat: The mechanical/posture claim is sensor-independent. No proprietary Blast metric is included. The source's internal-focus cue remains provenance, not default product policy, and the open tension with DRV1-001 is retained.

material_title: The Science Behind Hitting in Baseball with: Chad Miller
extracted_text: Hitting a baseball is a transfer of kinetic energy derived from the ground up, delivered sequentially through hips, shoulders, hands, and bat barrel while keeping the barrel behind the ball.
final_claim_text: Kinetic-chain energy transfer in a full-effort swing generally progresses sequentially from the ground up through the hips, torso, hands, and bat barrel.
observable_evidence: High-speed or slow-motion video showing the general sequence of ground drive, hip turn, trunk rotation, hand acceleration, and barrel delivery — as a qualitative pattern, not a precisely measured timing window.
coaching_cue: Drive from the ground up through hips, shoulders, and hands.
does_not_apply_when: Executing check swings, bunts, or emergency contact swings or adjustments.
source_side_caveat: This is qualitative podcast/interview commentary, not a peer-reviewed research finding. Observability is partial and qualitative; no SCI-001 numeric claims or rigid timing windows are included.

material_title: How To Coach Hitting Mechanics Pt. 1
extracted_text: Athletes produce more force and sequence more efficiently when focusing externally on movement outcomes rather than internally on body movements.
final_claim_text: External focus cues (focusing on ball flight or target outcome) promote superior force production and movement sequencing compared to internal focus cues (focusing on body mechanics).
observable_evidence: This is not a pattern directly observable in an individual swing clip. It is a cueing-policy principle for how coaching feedback is phrased, independent of what is observed in a specific analysis run.
coaching_cue: Focus on ball flight trajectory and where you want to hit the ball rather than internal body movement.
applies_when: Delivering verbal feedback during batting practice, cage work, or game preparation.
does_not_apply_when: Conducting explicit body-awareness drills or physical therapy screenings where internal focus is intentionally required.
source_side_caveat: Gemini verified that the source video displays research citations and that the presenter uses them to support the claim. HitterLoop has not independently audited the underlying papers; the research label records source-side cited support, not a completed paper-level literature review. The open cue-policy tension with BLM-001 remains explicit.
